topics.label: Course introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the multidisciplinary cancer biology lecture series and establishes the overarching learning objectives.

topics.label: Cellular origins, differentiation failure, and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics characterize cancer as a breakdown of developmental differentiation and genetic stability while exploring the histological and cell culture systems used to investigate tumor biology.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies using histological criteria and the colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma model.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the naming conventions for different tumor types and describe the physiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence patterns in humans and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare epidemiological cancer rates in human populations with tumor incidence across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical efficacy of cancer screening programs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale for early cancer detection and compare the methodologies, histological markers, and practical limitations of screening for different organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session outlook
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing directions for subsequent practicals and lectures.
